implemented_requirements.requirement: Player controls snake using directional inputs
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.handle_event maps pygame.KEYDOWN events to direction changes (arrow keys and WASD) and calls Snake.update_direction (game.py, lines handling direction_map).
Snake.move updates the head position based on the pending direction and updates the body list (snake.py). Game._step calls snake.move each tick.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Food items appear and can be eaten
implemented_requirements.evidence: Food.spawn places a food item on a random free cell (food.py). Game._step checks if new_head equals food position and triggers consumption.
When food is consumed, Game._step calls snake.grow(), which sets grow_pending; the next move keeps the tail, effectively growing the snake (snake.py).
Game._step calls snake.check_self_collision() and sets game_over if true (game.py).
Game._step checks new_head coordinates against GRID_WIDTH/GRID_HEIGHT and sets game_over on out‑of‑bounds (game.py).
Main loop calls game.render each frame; render draws board, food, snake and score bar via ui helpers (main.py & game.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Show current score based on food eaten
implemented_requirements.evidence: Score is incremented by SCORE_PER_FOOD on food consumption and drawn in draw_score_bar (ui.py).
settings.DIFFICULTIES defines Easy/Medium/Hard; main menu lets the player select a difficulty; Game uses the selected level to set move_interval_ms (settings.py, main.py, game.py).

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a functional classic Snake game: directional input handling, movement, food spawning, growth, collision detection, scoring, and a difficulty selection menu. Rendering of the board, snake, food, and UI elements is present. No major missing functionality or syntax errors are evident, making the implementation likely executable and meeting the benchmark requirements.
